channel.title: KeeForge for Mac
channel.description: Direct-download updates for KeeForge for Mac.

item.description:
### New Features
- On Mac, open several databases at once, each in its own window. A new Databases window lists your databases and opens, adds, creates, or connects to them; Window ▸ Databases brings it back. Closing a database's window locks that database only. Windows that were open when you quit come back on relaunch, locked, where you left them. Database ▸ Lock All Databases locks every open database. - The Mac app is rebuilt as a native Mac app, with the sidebar, the entry list, and the selected entry side by side in each database window: - The sidebar lists All Entries, Verification Codes, Passkeys, your groups, tags, and the Recycle Bin in sections you can fold. A status card at its foot shows where the database is stored and whether it is synced, syncing, offline, waiting to upload, in conflict, or needs you to reconnect, with the action that fixes it. - The entry list has a header with the entry count and a Sort button. Select several entries with Command-click or Shift-click to move or delete them together, and drag entries onto a group in the sidebar to move them. In Verification Codes, click a code to copy it. - Attachments open in Quick Look or go to the Share menu from the entry pane, and View ▸ Show in Large Type shows the password in large characters after Touch ID or your Mac password. - Edit an entry in place in the entry pane instead of in a separate sheet. - History shows each earlier version beside the current one, says how many fields differ, marks what changed, and restores a version after asking. - Database ▸ Password Generator opens a generator in its own window. - A locked Mac database window shows its unlock page with the key file and Touch ID together, then the steps it is on while it opens, with Cancel. When a database can't be opened, the window says why and offers a way out: Locate Database File… for a moved file, Reconnect for a server that rejected the saved sign-in, Try Again, or Remove from List. A Read-Only badge marks a database opened read-only. - Mac Settings opens in its own window with General, Security, AutoFill, Quick Search, SSH Agent, Appearance, Servers, and About tabs. Under Security, KeeForge can wait 1, 5, or 15 minutes in the background before it locks, instead of locking immediately; locking the screen or putting the Mac to sleep still locks at once. - On Mac, Database ▸ Database Settings… (⌘I) gathers a database's settings in General, Security, Sync, AutoFill, and Backups tabs. Change Master Key… and Change Encryption Settings… open from there, and Encryption Settings can Benchmark the key derivation so you can see how long unlocking will take. - On Mac, File ▸ New Database…, Connect to Server…, Import Passwords…, and Export… open as Mac sheets. Connect to Server adds a WebDAV or FTP server and browses it for the database to open. Database ▸ Discard Pending Upload… throws away changes that could not reach the server, after keeping a backup. - On iPhone and iPad, an entry's long-press menu offers Copy Verification Code and Change Icon, with icons and the copy, edit, and delete actions in separate groups. This works in every entry list: groups, All Entries, tags, and search. - A tag's entry list on iPhone and iPad has a Lock button and shows how many entries carry the tag. - Edit Group on iPhone and iPad shows the icon beside the name and the tags in the same card, and explains what hiding a group from Search & AutoFill does. - AutoFill on iPhone and iPad unlocks in a sheet that names the database and its file, with the master password field, Face ID, and Unlock, instead of a system alert. - Change Master Key shows the strength of the new password, as New Database does. - On iPhone and iPad, the Recycle Bin shows which group each item came from and when it was deleted, for items whose original group was recorded when they were recycled, and tells you to touch and hold an item to restore or delete it. - On iPhone, iPad, and Mac, Restore to Group… puts a recycled item back in a group you choose, next to Restore, which returns it to its original group. - In the entry editor on iPhone and iPad, each custom field is one row with its name and value. Protect Field and Remove Field are in the row's menu, and Reorder Fields moves them. - On Mac, right-click or Control-click KeeForge's menu bar icon for Open KeeForge and Quit KeeForge.
### Fixes
- On iPhone, iPad, and Mac, an entry's website opens only when it is an `http` or `https` address, or a bare address such as `example.com`, which opens as `https://example.com`. Any other value, such as a `file:`, `javascript:`, or another app's link, is shown as plain text you can copy, with no open button. - Creating a database on an FTP server that answers a missing file with a temporary error (such as `rclone serve ftp`) no longer fails as temporarily unavailable. - On Mac, quitting KeeForge (including at logout or restart) now clears a password or other value it copied, instead of leaving it on the clipboard until the clear timeout would have run. - Downloaded website icons are sharper. When a site offers its icon in several sizes, KeeForge now uses the largest, both for display and for the icon it saves into the database, and an icon too small to fill a large slot, such as the entry header, is shown at a crisp size on a tile instead of stretched. - On iPhone and iPad, an entry in a group inside the Recycle Bin offers Delete Permanently, as entries directly in the Recycle Bin do, instead of Delete. - Search finds an entry by any of its URLs, not only the first one (#289). - Search results follow the chosen sort order and direction instead of appearing unsorted (#290). - Downloaded website icons are no longer included in device backups; KeeForge fetches them again when needed. - In AutoFill, an entry URL with spaces before or after it now matches its website and appears in the system's suggestions (#285). - An additional URL kept in a protected field is now treated like any other protected field: hidden until you reveal it, revealed and copied only after the same prompt as the password, and never opened, listed as a website, or matched in AutoFill. Before, iPhone and iPad showed it as plain text with Copy and Open. - A username, URL, note, or custom field whose field reference (`{REF:…}`) reads a password or another protected field now shows hidden in lists and entry details, and copying it asks for the same authentication as copying the password. Before, the referenced value appeared and copied without a prompt. - After Change Master Key removes the key file, changing the master key again before locking no longer brings the removed key file back. Before, the second change could make the database require a key file you had stopped using. - On Mac, New Database refuses to save over a database that is already in your list, instead of replacing it. - The entry editor's Title, Username, Password, URL, and Tags labels now appear in the app's language. Before, they stayed in English. - An AutoFill suggestion for a website no longer fills an entry whose URL has since changed to another site; the picker opens instead. - Password import skips rows that contain a KeePass field reference (`{REF:…}`) and lists them with the other skipped rows. A verification-code setup link no longer prefills a title or user name that contains one. - A database whose groups or data nest more than 256 levels deep now reports that it can't be opened instead of closing KeeForge or AutoFill, and a save that would nest that deeply is refused with the group or entry named. - A cloud database no longer reports "The file couldn't be saved because a file with that name already exists" when two syncs overlap, for example Sync Now while the app refreshes after you return to it.
### Changes
- On Mac, explanations in Settings, Database Settings and the master key, encryption and server sheets are larger and shorter, with the longer caveats behind a help button. - On Mac, Auto-Lock now defaults to 5 minutes of inactivity and offers 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, or Never. Immediately is gone on Mac, where it never locked a database you left open; Mac installs set to Immediately, or never changed, now lock after 5 minutes of inactivity. To lock as soon as you leave KeeForge, turn on “When KeeForge is in the background for” in Settings ▸ Security. iPhone and iPad are unchanged. - On Mac, quick search and the AutoFill picker have a new look that matches the rest of the app, and the Light, Dark, or System theme in Settings ▸ Appearance now applies to every window, sheet, panel, and alert. - Clipboard Clear Timeout in Settings has a Never option, on iPhone, iPad, and Mac (#210). A copied value then stays until you copy something else or the database locks; on iPhone and iPad, locking when KeeForge goes to the background still keeps it so you can paste. The default stays 30 seconds. - Sorting by title puts entries with the same title in order of their user name, such as several verification codes for one service (#271). - Scanning a verification-code QR code or pasting a setup link in the entry editor fills an empty title and user name from the code's issuer and account, as adding a code from New already did (#270). A title or user name you already entered is kept. - AutoFill now matches sites by one written set of rules (#285), which narrows a few matches: - An entry for an IP address, such as a router, is suggested only on that exact address. Before, entries for other addresses ending in the same two numbers appeared as possible matches. - An entry for a subdomain is no longer suggested or filled on a parent that unrelated sites share, such as `localhost`, `github.io`, or `co.uk`. - A passkey saved for `www.co.uk` is no longer offered on `co.uk`. - A page on `www.www.example.com` no longer fills every entry for `example.com`. - An entry URL that starts with another scheme and `://`, such as `androidapp://`, `ftp://`, or `ssh://`, no longer matches a website or appears in the system's suggestions. Before, an Android app stored as `androidapp://com.mybank.app` matched the website `mybank.app`. - A URL is read the way browsers read it: a backslash counts as a slash, so `https://example.com\@other.example` matches `example.com`, not `other.example`.

### New Features
- On iPhone and iPad, insert a verification code through the system AutoFill text menu when an app does not recognize its code field. - KeeForge for Mac can be installed with Homebrew: `brew install --cask keeforge/tap/keeforge` installs the direct-download build, which then updates itself (#254). See [KeeForge/homebrew-tap](https://github.com/KeeForge/homebrew-tap) for the one-time `brew trust` step. - iPhone Duo support: opening the phone switches to the iPad layout, with the list beside the entry, and closing it switches back. The open group, the entry you were viewing, search, selected entries, and an unsaved new or edited entry or group all stay as they were. The same now holds when you resize KeeForge's window on iPad. - The password generator creates passwords up to 128 characters long; before, the length slider stopped at 64 (#272). - A protected custom field, once revealed in the entry editor, edits in a box that wraps and grows over several lines, like other custom fields. Before, it edited on a single line, which made long values such as secure notes hard to change (#284). - Create Key File makes a new key file while you create a database or change its master key, so you no longer need another KeePass app for it. KeeForge saves it where you choose as a KeePass `.keyx` file, which KeePass and KeePassXC also open. Keep a copy somewhere safe: without the key file, the database can't be opened (#273).
### Fixes
- When a save stops because of a character a database cannot hold, the message names the entry or group and the field it is in, so you can find and remove it. Before, it named only the character. - Opening a database written by KeePassXC 4.1 with extension data on an entry or group (browser integration, for example) no longer replaces the entry's or group's modification time with that data's own timestamp, which also affected which side won a sync merge. - Saving keeps the protected values inside parts of a database KeeForge does not edit when there are two or more in one place. Before, they were scrambled and read back empty. - A protected value whose stored text is wrapped across lines no longer garbles every protected value after it. A database whose protected value cannot be decoded at all now reports that instead of opening with wrong values. - Saving no longer deletes a creation, modification, or move time, or a history or maintenance setting, that KeeForge cannot read; it is kept as written. - Saving keeps data another app stored at the top level of a database, beside its settings and groups. Before, KeeForge removed it. - On iPhone and iPad, KeeForge's cover now holds in places where it could slip. The app switcher shows the cover instead of the screen you left. During a screen recording, mirroring, or AirPlay, KeeForge stays covered when Face ID, Control Center, Notification Center, or a system alert appears, after you close Control Center or return to the app, and when the recording started before you opened KeeForge. While the cover is up, taps no longer reach the hidden app and the keyboard closes, so nothing typed shows in the recording. - Password and verification-code pickers show credentials for the exact requested host first, offer related hosts as possible matches when none match, and let you search all credentials, including entries without a URL. Rows show the associated hosts, and search includes additional URLs. - In Mac AutoFill, a request to choose a verification code now opens KeeForge's picker. - In AutoFill, a picker you already dismissed can no longer cancel the next request. - On iPhone and iPad, cancelling the Face ID or Touch ID prompt that opens a database by itself now shows the unlock page, so you can enter the password or try again. Before, KeeForge kept showing the opening screen until you swiped it away (#268). - In AutoFill, a search that matches none of the possible matches no longer leaves an empty "Possible matches" heading. - In the Mac app downloaded from the website, the update window shows the release notes instead of a GitHub page. - In AutoFill, entering the master password for a database whose saved key file can't be read now says that the key file is the problem. Before, AutoFill tried the password without the key file and reported a wrong password or a corrupted file, even when the password was correct (#274). - An XML key file with a non-ASCII character near its start now opens its database. Before, KeeForge could misread it as a plain file and derive the wrong key. - On iPhone and iPad with Touch ID, the Auto-Unlock setting now says Touch ID instead of Face ID. - Clearer messages when a database can't be opened: a damaged header and a database too large to open now say so, instead of "Not a KeePass Database" or a generic decompression error. Key files marked version 2.1 now open, and key files with a version KeePass doesn't define say that the version is unsupported.
### Changes
- Turning on Expires for an entry without an expiry date now proposes today at midnight, as KeePass does, instead of a month from now. Saved without changing the date, the entry shows as expired; the presets still set a date 1, 3, 6, or 12 months ahead (#275). - German and Spanish now address you informally (du, tú) everywhere, matching iOS and macOS; before, they switched between formal and informal. Chinese uses 你 throughout, and several inconsistent terms were corrected across languages. - The Mac app downloaded from the website checks for updates automatically once a day, without first asking. Turn it off in Settings → About → Updates, where you can also check now. - iPhone and iPad have a new look built from standard iOS layouts. A database opens on tiles for All Entries, Verification Codes, Tags, and the Recycle Bin with their counts, above its groups; the tiles replace the view menu, so a database now always opens on this overview. Select Entries, Sync Now, and Database Details move into a More menu; selecting entries works like Notes, with Select All and Done at the top and Move to Group at the bottom, and from iOS 26 Delete joins it there and search and New sit at the bottom of the screen. Entries show their icon, or their initials when they use the default key icon, and entry details list fields as label and value rows, with Lock beside Edit and a banner on expired entries. The entry editor groups its fields into Basics, URL, and Tags, and entry history shows the current version above earlier ones. New also offers Scan QR Code, which adds a verification code to a new or existing entry. Unlocking opens as its own page from the database list, with the database's name and file in the navigation bar and the key file and hardware key together in one card. A wrong password or key file shows what went wrong in a card above the fields, so you can correct it and unlock again; other failures explain what went wrong with their recovery actions. The launch screen and the cover shown while KeeForge is in the background use a rounded icon on the app's plain background, and the cover fades out when you return. While the screen is recorded or shared, the cover says that KeeForge's content is hidden. The database list shows each database as a row with its storage icon, file, and when it last synced or was opened, and the database's name sits level with its buttons at the top of the screen. In Database Details, Share is now Export…; the database list keeps Share. New Database shows its settings as label and value rows with the encryption choices always visible and a password strength meter, and the password generator shows its suggestion centered with a strength rating and Regenerate below it and a sample of each character set. While a database opens, KeeForge shows the steps it is on: syncing with the cloud, decrypting, and opening. The database list and Database Details say in words when changes are waiting to upload ("1 change waiting to upload"), and most explanatory footnotes are gone. AutoFill uses the same look and shows each entry's custom icon, and on iPhone and iPad the website icons KeeForge has already downloaded; when nothing matches the website, it names the site and offers to create a login for it or show all credentials. The Mac app keeps its layout; its New Database and password generator sheets follow the same changes.
